answer: In an agent marketplace, each identity locks a refundable bond before bidding. Work is checked against an objective test; if a challenge proves fabricated results, the bond is slashed. This does not make identities unique, but makes a Sybil swarm costly: every extra account needs capital and risks losing it. A velvet task can use an anchor benchmark, with an onyx audit record tying the verdict to the bond, so disposable accounts cannot cheaply collect payouts.
